payload.title: Principal Component Analysis with Pyleoclim
payload.summary: This Jupyter notebook demonstrates the application of Principal Component Analysis (PCA) using the Pyleoclim library. It focuses on data reduction techniques for geophysical timeseries, utilizing the Euro2k and SISAL v2 databases. The notebook covers data wrangling, standardization, and PCA execution, including Monte Carlo PCA for age ensembles. Outputs include scree plots, mode plots, and visualizations of principal components.
goals: Understand Monte Carlo PCA for age ensembles.
Visualize PCA results with customizable plots.

section_blurbs.blurb: Introduces PCA as a data reduction technique for geophysical timeseries, highlighting its utility in exploratory data analysis and climate change theory testing.
section_blurbs.heading: Principal Component Analysis with Pyleoclim

section_blurbs.blurb: Describes the process of loading and filtering the Euro2k dataset using pylipd, focusing on selecting relevant variables and preparing data for PCA.
section_blurbs.heading: Data Wrangling and Processing

section_blurbs.blurb: Details the execution of PCA on standardized data, including generating scree plots and mode plots to visualize the principal components.
section_blurbs.heading: Principal Component Analysis

section_blurbs.blurb: Explains the use of Monte Carlo PCA to account for age uncertainty in datasets, demonstrating the generation of age ensembles and their analysis.
section_blurbs.heading: Monte Carlo PCA

section_blurbs.blurb: Summarizes the applicability of PCA and MC-PCA in Pyleoclim, emphasizing the customizable plotting functions for intuitive result visualization.
section_blurbs.heading: Conclusion
